claims.text: The starting material consists of W particles or connected W regions within a Cu matrix.
Optimized spark-plasma sintering can minimize void formation in W-Cu composites.
Spark-plasma sintering uses rapid electrical heating and applied pressure to consolidate powders.
Adjusting spark-plasma sintering parameters can control the resulting microstructure or phase constitution.
Optimized spark-plasma sintering will produce a uniform W-Cu composite.
Reducing void formation will improve thermal transport in the W-Cu composite.
Reducing void formation will improve the mechanical durability of the W-Cu composite.
The optimized spark-plasma-sintered W-Cu composite will have 20% higher thermal conductivity than a conventionally induction- or arc-plasma-cast composite.
The optimized spark-plasma-sintered W-Cu composite will have 15% higher mechanical strength than a conventionally induction- or arc-plasma-cast composite.
Casting refractory, high-melting-point alloy systems can cause incomplete melting, chemical heterogeneity, casting defects, and coarse microstructures.
Powder-metallurgy processing can produce more homogeneous microstructures and mechanical properties comparable or superior to ingot metallurgy.
The proposed processing boundary is 2000-2500 °C and 50-100 MPa.
The composite is intended to operate at high temperature under irradiation.
The exact optimal spark-plasma sintering parameters are unknown and require experimental determination.
Failure to obtain at least a 10% thermal-conductivity increase and a 5% mechanical-strength increase relative to casting would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies 20% higher thermal conductivity and 15% higher strength, but the falsification rule accepts increases of only 10% and 5%. Results between those values would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
